definitions.explanation: Snow falling from the sky, or the amount of snow that has fallen. A formal term used in weather reports, news, and official contexts.

examples.japanese: {昨夜|さくや}から{降雪|こうせつ}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: Snowfall has continued since last night.

examples.japanese: {降雪|こうせつ}の{影響|えいきょう}で{電車|でんしゃ}が{遅延|ちえん}している。
examples.english: Trains are delayed due to snowfall.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}は{降雪量|こうせつりょう}が{例年|れいねん}の{二倍|にばい}を{超|こ}えた{地域|ちいき}もある。
examples.english: There are areas where snowfall this year has exceeded double the usual amount.

notes:
Compound of {降|こう} (to fall/descend) + {雪|せつ} (snow). A formal, written term commonly seen in weather forecasts and news reports.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {降雪量|こうせつりょう} (amount of snowfall)
- {降雪|こうせつ}{地域|ちいき} (snowfall area)
- {大量|たいりょう}の{降雪|こうせつ} (heavy snowfall)
- {降雪|こうせつ}の{影響|えいきょう} (effects of snowfall)

USAGE NOTE:
In everyday conversation, people say {雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}る (it snows) rather than using {降雪|こうせつ}. {降雪|こうせつ} belongs to the formal register of weather terminology, similar to {降水|こうすい} (precipitation).
